articleHeadline: Doctors caution against indiscriminate antibiotic use as monsoon-related illnesses rise
articleSummary: Doctors caution against indiscriminate antibiotic use as monsoon-related illnesses rise. With fever as a common symptom, clinicians warn that fever does not reliably indicate a bacterial infection and self-medication with antibiotics can fuel antimicrobial resistance. Viral illnesses, dengue, malaria, typhoid and other conditions can cause fever, and treatment should be guided by clinical assessment, duration of illness, associated symptoms, and appropriate diagnostic investigations. Patients often present after taking multiple medicines, including antibiotics, simply because they have fever; the first step is to determine the underlying cause rather than reflexively prescribing antibiotics. articleSummary: A swine flu (H1N1) infection is described as causing stomach issues in children, in addition to respiratory symptoms. articleSummary: West Nile fever has reached Brazil’s São Paulo with its first reported cases, while Santa Catarina records the country’s first death. articleSummary: Critical Phase of Dengue Fever: In Indonesia, the critical phase of dengue begins 3–7 days after fever onset, with the highest risk around days 4–5. Lasting 24–48 hours, this phase involves increased vascular permeability and plasma leakage into body cavities, risking hypovolemic shock. Many families feel relieved when the fever subsides and discharge patients, but the critical phase often starts as the fever wanes. Monitoring is essential per Indonesian guidelines (RI MOH 2024; PAPDI 2023; WHO). Warning signs include severe, persistent abdominal pain; intractable vomiting (especially as fever falls); restlessness or reduced consciousness; sudden bleeding (nosebleeds, gum, hematemesis, melena); cold, clammy extremities with sweating; and signs of shock with a weak, fast pulse. Tests: rising hematocrit (≥20% from baseline) and platelets <100,000/mm³; ultrasound may show free fluid. Treatment: hospital-based IV crystalloids (e.g., Ringer lactate/acetate); possible platelet transfusion for active bleeding. Recovery follows the critical phase.
